# ⚡ Instant Play — research & verification report

**Date:** 2 November 2026 · **Branch:** `arena/2dc0feb1-tabulous-games` · **Source of truth:** [`instant-play.json`](instant-play.json) · **Generated by:** `scripts/build.mjs` (the tables below are regenerated from the JSON; edit the JSON, not this file).

The brief was to discover, research, verify and actually integrate as many *instant-play* browser games as possible, add a prominent **⚡ INSTANT PLAY** section at the very top of the games page above all existing games, preserve the existing 79-port catalogue, and be extremely thorough. The primary success criterion was later clarified as **clicking a game and immediately playing it on a desktop Chrome browser**.

---

## 1. Scope, method, sources and verification limits

**Research first.** The starting points were the two named articles — [TweakTown, 8 Oct 2026: "You can now play Skate 3, Black Ops and 20-plus classic games in your web browser"](https://www.tweaktown.com/news/113993/you-can-now-play-skate-3-black-ops-and-20-plus-classic-games-in-your-web-browser/index.html) and [XDA: "AAA games are playable in web browsers with AI-based reverse engineering"](https://www.xda-developers.com/aaa-games-are-playable-in-web-browsers-with-ai-based-reverse-engineering/) — followed by the takedown follow-up [TweakTown, 11 Oct 2026](https://www.tweaktown.com/news/114029/activision-takes-down-ai-made-black-ops-2-browser-ports/index.html). From there the research covered `ported2browser.com`, `wasm.rip`, `portedgames.com`, `browsergame.si`, `justplayweb.com`, `dos.zone`, `vel.gg/bsz`, the Skate 3 / SHAR / decompilation port pages, the Internet Archive's MS-DOS Software Library and Internet Arcade, ScummWEB/ScummVM, Cloudflare's WebAssembly Doom experiment, official rights-holder browser releases, and the open-source web-game ecosystem.

**Verify second.** All 155 playable Internet Archive identifiers were confirmed to exist against the Archive's own `advancedsearch.php` API (`collection:softwarelibrary_msdos_games`, `subject:shareware`, `subject:freeware`, and `collection:internetarcade`). All 7 ScummWEB `/play` pages were fetched and returned their "ScummVM loaded / starting …" launch UI. Every official and open-source destination (Minecraft Classic, Google's Pac-Man Doodle, official Tetris, 2048, A Dark Room, Hextris, Sandspiel, BeepBox, shapez, NetHack/alt.org, DCSS, Pokémon Showdown, Lichess, Cloudflare's Doom) was fetched individually and its launch/library UI observed. Two dead or hostile destinations were found and **excluded**: `www.quakejs.com` returns Cloudflare error 526 (invalid SSL), and the former `freecivweb.org` domain now serves unrelated gambling spam. `dos.zone` was unreachable from the research environment and is not linked.

**Honest limit.** The build sandbox has **no Chrome/Chromium binary** — `command -v chromium chromium-browser google-chrome firefox` returns nothing, and the only DOM library available (`jsdom`) cannot run WebGL, WebGPU, WebAssembly or DOS emulation. Therefore no game was observed *rendering* end-to-end here. Every playable row is marked `verification: "link-verified"` (destination exists, resolves, is correctly attributed and needs no download), **not** "play-tested". Mobile, touch and gamepad behaviour are recorded as `unverified` rather than promised. The site states this plainly on every section. That is why unlicensed AAA ports with uncertain asset provenance were not given play buttons at all.

**Implement third, test fourth.** A safe version-control checkpoint (`41e57df`) was committed before the site was touched. The integration adds a generated `INSTANT` block directly after `<main>`, reuses the existing design tokens and the existing inline script, and leaves every pre-existing generated block (`HERO`, `CATEGORY-PILLS`, `STATUS-PILLS`, `SOURCE-PILLS`, `GAMES`) byte-for-byte unchanged. `npm run check` (build determinism, 79-cover artwork audit, structural/ID checks, instant-play honesty guards) and a 62-assertion `jsdom` DOM suite both pass; the local server returns HTTP 200.

## 7. Most impressive discoveries

1. **The Internet Archive's EM-DOSBox MS-DOS Software Library** — 8,943 items playable in Chrome with no install, including 116 `subject:shareware` and 47 `subject:freeware` titles. This is the single biggest legitimate source of recognisable classics: Doom, Wolfenstein 3D, Duke Nukem 3D, Commander Keen, Raptor, Blake Stone, Bio Menace, Crystal Caves, Epic Pinball, Death Rally, Prince of Persia, SimCity, Civilization, Monkey Island, Maniac Mansion, Oregon Trail, Tomb Raider, Rayman and Mortal Kombat all start in a browser tab.
2. **The Internet Archive's Internet Arcade** — 2,663 arcade boards preserved and playable through JSMESS/Emularity: Out Run, Defender, Joust, Q\*bert, Dig Dug, Tron, Centipede, Marble Madness, Pengo, Paperboy, Commando, Root Beer Tapper, Congo Bongo, Mr. Do!, Berzerk and more.
3. **ScummVM compiled to WebAssembly** — ScummWEB hosts seven *publisher-released freeware* adventures (Beneath a Steel Sky, Drascula, DreamWeb, Lure of the Temptress, Nippon Safes, Flight of the Amazon Queen, Broken Sword 2.5), each with a readme/licence link and a one-click `/play` page.
4. **Cloudflare's Silent Space Marine Doom** — a WebAssembly Doom port running on Workers, Durable Objects and WebSockets, with a "Play Solo" path that needs no WAD import.
5. **Official, no-account releases** — Mojang's Minecraft Classic (WebGL), Google's officially licensed 2010 Pac-Man Doodle, and the Tetris Company's free browser Tetris.
6. **Open-source web-native games** — 2048, A Dark Room, Hextris, Sandspiel, BeepBox, shapez Demo, NetHack via alt.org's hterm, Dungeon Crawl Stone Soup WebTiles, Pokémon Showdown and Lichess — all free, account-free and legitimate.
7. **On the AAA side (research only):** a Rust/Bevy WebAssembly + WebGPU engine for Skate 3, a decompilation-based Halo: Combat Evolved browser build, Xash3D-based Half-Life, and the N64 decomp family (Super Mario 64, Ocarina of Time, Majora's Mask, Perfect Dark, Diddy Kong Racing, Donkey Kong 64, Conker). Technically remarkable — but they need your own game files or distribute someone else's.

| Call of Duty: Black Ops / BO2 Zombies (`vel.gg`, `/bo1z`, `/bsz`) | Activision sent a DMCA notice to Cloudflare on 19 Oct 2026; `/bo1z` now shows "Unavailable for legal reasons". The viral build streamed Activision's own maps, models and animations (roughly 271–590 MB per map), needed cross-origin isolation and could not be iframed. No lawful no-copy release exists. |
| Call of Duty: Black Ops II (AI-assisted ports) | DMCA'd by Activision on 11 Oct 2026 for exporting retail maps, models and animations. |
| Skate 3 (`skate.aaddpp.lol`) | Rust/Bevy clean-room engine, but the public build asks for **your own converted copy** of Skate 3. That is a browser port, not instant play. Classified BROWSER PORT; needs Chrome/Edge 113+ with WebGPU and hardware acceleration. |
| The Simpsons: Hit & Run (WASM) | Streams ~3.6 GB of the 2003 game's data from its own server, reportedly derived from source leaked in 2021, with no authorisation from Disney/Vivendi. |
| Need for Speed: Most Wanted / Underground 2, Resident Evil 4, Tekken 5, Cuphead, GTA V, Cyberpunk 2077 on `ported2browser.com` / `wasm.rip` | Unlicensed WebAssembly ports that fetch retail assets over HTTPS. XDA's own source describes the legal position as "Absolutely not". GTA V's `playgta5.com` build vanished within hours of going up on 6 Oct 2026. |
| GTA III / Vice City (DOS Zone, re3/reVC) | Take-Two DMCA'd DOS Zone's Vice City in December 2025 **even though** it required the user's own files. Open-source re3/reVC reimplementations are classified BROWSER PORT because you must supply the original assets. |
| Super Mario 64, Zelda OoT/MM, Perfect Dark, Diddy Kong Racing, Donkey Kong 64, Conker, Pilotwings 64 | Decompilation/recompilation ports that rebuild *code* only. Super Mario 64's browser build was changed to require a user-supplied ROM after the DMCA wave. These are the same model as the 79 native ports already in the directory — one-time setup with your own files, not click-and-play. |
| Half-Life, Counter-Strike 1.6, Quake III Arena, Halo CE, Tomb Raider (OpenLara), PES 6 | Engine reimplementations that need the original game data from a legal installation; no rights-holder browser release. |
| Minecraft 1.8.8 (Eaglercraft) | Unofficial fan port, not endorsed by Mojang. Minecraft Classic above is the official, account-free alternative. |
| Portal: The Flash Version, Super Mario 63, Ultimate Flash Sonic, 3D Pinball Space Cadet | Listed in the research database as INSTANT PLAY but kept out of the grid because the only launch pages found belong to a portal that also carries unlicensed AAA ports. Not presented as verified until an independent lawful host is confirmed. |
| Xbox Cloud Gaming, GeForce NOW, Amazon Luna | Genuine **STREAMING** (video rendered on a remote machine), not locally browser-executed games, and all require an account plus a paid subscription. Deliberately separated in the research table and the site legend. |
| QuakeJS (`www.quakejs.com`), Freeciv-web, DOS Zone | QuakeJS returns Cloudflare 526 invalid SSL; `freecivweb.org` has been taken over by gambling spam; DOS Zone was unreachable. Dead links were not added. |
| Burnout 3, Tony Hawk, Spider-Man, Crash, Spyro, Prince of Persia (console), Sonic/Mario/Zelda/Pokémon (console), Street Fighter, Mortal Kombat (console originals) | No authorised browser release found during this pass. Where a legitimate MS-DOS or arcade version exists, that version is in the playable grid instead. |

## 9. Remaining technical and legal restrictions

* **No game files are hosted here.** This repository contains no ROMs, ISOs, BIOS images, WADs, installers, executables or game assets. Every play button opens a third-party host in a new tab (or its own embeddable player). Rights holders should contact the host, and we will remove any link on request.
* **Library-hosted preservation copies are not the same as public domain.** Many Internet Archive MS-DOS and arcade items are still in copyright and are offered by the Archive under its own preservation and takedown policies. The grid filters to shareware, publisher-released freeware, open-source projects, official releases, and Archive-hosted preservation copies; each card states its licence class. This is a linking/curation position, not a licence grant.
* **"Asset streaming" is not cloud gaming.** WebAssembly/WebGPU ports that fetch retail game data into your browser execute **locally** on your machine. They are classified separately from `STREAMING` services (Xbox Cloud Gaming, GeForce NOW, Luna) where the game runs on a remote server and only video/input cross the network.
* **Embedding is up to the host.** `archive.org/embed/<identifier>` and the ScummWEB `/play` pages are designed for embedding; other hosts may send `X-Frame-Options` / CSP headers that block it. The in-page player therefore always offers a clearly labelled **"Open on host ↗"** fallback and explains what to do if the frame stays blank. No fake loading screens or misleading play buttons are used.
* **Emulation needs a moment and a keyboard.** EM-DOSBox and JSMESS download the game data on first start; DOS and arcade titles expect keyboard input. Chrome on desktop is the supported target. Mobile/touch/gamepad compatibility is marked **untested**, not promised.
* **Some official games have requirements.** Minecraft Classic needs WebGL/WebRTC and a keyboard; the fetch environment could only report its "keyboard required" gate. ScummVM freeware titles download a few megabytes on first launch. 2048's original GitHub Pages host now redirects to `play2048.co`.
* **No end-to-end rendering verification.** The sandbox has no browser binary. `verification: "link-verified"` means the destination exists and is honestly described; it does not mean the game was observed running. `npm run links:instant` is provided so the catalogue can be re-verified from a machine with normal internet access.
* **Unlicensed AAA ports remain off the grid permanently** unless a rights holder authorises them. Recent DMCA actions against Black Ops II, GTA Vice City and GTA V browser builds make that the only defensible position.
* **GitHub Actions.** As in the previous task, the `Verify catalogue` workflow fails at runner startup with `steps: 0`; GitHub Pages builds and all local checks succeed. This is an infrastructure issue, not a failing test.
